recorded-direction.text: The diagram draws design direction, executable model, reviewed contract and production implementation vertically as distinct stages. The later stages remain unproved. Decisions preserve own-anchor independence, institutional publication as an explicit trust option, and availability purchased separately from authority.

named-deployment-roles.text: Anchors and ledgers run nodes. Anchors serve signed roots; ledgers serve data and proofs. Applications serve application proofs. Terminals consume all three, verify them and build transactions or drive real-world effects. The names describe roles rather than a fixed deployment count.

words-that-constrain-the-design.text: The project separates immutable hashed content from chain indexes. Anchors publish roots for every block. Proof-bearing answers bind to an externally supplied root; later discussion clarified that reconstruction transactions may arrive without individual proofs.

Ledger proofs are checked off-chain and are not placed in transaction redeemers. Application proofs are placed in redeemers. Cardano checks actual ledger validity, and application validators check the application proofs.

Ledger proof values concern on-chain validity in the present, at the selected chainpoint. Application proof values concern on-chain validation of a proposed future transaction. This temporal distinction does not promise that an old state stays current or that a future transaction succeeds.

what-remains-unproved.text: The commitment inventory, completeness proofs, historical reconstruction coverage, root publication policy and session behavior still need contracts and evidence. Anchor and ledger costs require separate measurements. Switching and availability commitments need acceptance demonstrations; market efficiency remains a thesis.

evidence-available-today.text: MPFS already verifies reconstructed facts against an anchored state root. The inspected Koios and Blockfrost interfaces do not promise the required shared chainpoint sessions. Related root-signing work is not evidence that the whole publication protocol exists.
